paper.title_en: Analysis of <math display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>τ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub></math> decays in a <math display="inline"><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> and scalar leptoquark model
paper.abstract_en: Motivated by the recent anomalies related to <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>l</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></math> decays, we perform a theoretical investigation to search for new physics in <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> decays through <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></math> and scalar LQ model. We have studied <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>τ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></math> decays, which involve a <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>τ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></math> quark level transition. To fix the values of the new coupling parameters, we performed <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>χ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> fitting using experimental results of <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>*</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>π</mi><mi>l</mi></msubsup></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, and <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Incorporating the best fit values of new coupling parameters, we have calculated values of the branching ratios, the lepton flavor nonuniversalities ratios, the lepton longitudinal polarization asymmetry, the lepton hadron polarization asymmetry, the forward backward asymmetry, and the ratio of the partially integrated decay rate of <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>p</mi><mi>τ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></math> over the <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mi>τ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">¯</mo></mover><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></math>. Except for forward-backward asymmetry and leptonic hadron polarization asymmetry, some observables show significant deviations, while others show slight inconsistencies with their standard model predicted values.
